advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide/handle the finish_reason='error' (retryable StructuredOutputError) case in guard_capability so a transient error is not turned into an un-retried run abort, and document the chosen behavior.
evidence: structured.py:647-648 — `if stop_reason in _BAD_STOP_REASONS: raise StructuredOutputError(...)` (the transient `error` finish_reason path)
structured.py:623: `"error": "the model run ended in an error (finish_reason=error)"`
structured_run.py:176: `except StructuredOutputError as exc:` then re-prompts and loops — the prior path treats a retryable StructuredOutputError from check_response as a retry, not an abort
ABSENCE: no test exercises a finish_reason='error' turn through guard_capability to pin its (non-retrying) behavior
advisory.finding: In guard_capability's after_model_request hook, check_response can raise a *retryable* plain StructuredOutputError (finish_reason='error', see structured.py:647-648). Because that is not a ModelRetry, Pydantic AI aborts the run rather than driving a bounded retry — diverging from the prior structured_run loop, which caught plain StructuredOutputError and retried the call (structured_run.py:176-188). The 'error is retryable' semantic is silently lost when the guard raises it.
scenarios: A provider returns finish_reason='error' (transient run error) on the first turn; under the old loop this retried, under the guard it aborts the whole run with no retry

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a guard-capability test driving finish_reason='error' asserting the emitted error is the retryable StructuredOutputError (not the terminal UnretryableOutputError subtype).
evidence: structured.py:645-648: `if stop_reason in _UNRETRYABLE_STOP_REASONS: raise UnretryableOutputError(...)` then `if stop_reason in _BAD_STOP_REASONS: raise StructuredOutputError(...)` — 'error' is in _BAD_STOP_REASONS (structured.py:623) but NOT in _UNRETRYABLE_STOP_REASONS (structured.py:632), so it raises the retryable base type.

Guard tests only cover finish_reason='content_filter' (test line 190), 'length' (line 206), and provider_details refusal (line 218) — all UnretryableOutputError. ABSENCE: no test drives finish_reason='error' through guard_capability to assert the retryable StructuredOutputError branch the guard emits from after_model_request.
advisory.finding: The guard_capability path is untested for finish_reason='error', which structured.check_response/check_stop_reason maps to a RETRYABLE StructuredOutputError (not the terminal UnretryableOutputError). All guard tests exercise only the terminal subtypes (content_filter, length, provider_details refusal), leaving the retryable-vs-terminal branch of the changed behavior without regression coverage.
